Rhizopus shows dark black sporangia - very different from the test image's translucent spores. The test image strongly resembles Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold) with its round, clustered conidia on branching conidiophores. Let me check a few more classes.

The test image (Bugwood ID 5530077) is clearly a microscopic view showing round, translucent conidia clustered in grape-like arrangements on branching conidiophores - the hallmark of Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold). The Rhizopus showed dark black sporangia (very different), Powdery Mildew shows chains (not grape clusters), and Alternaria shows black spores.

The Gray Mold reference (Bugwood_32) showed fluffy gray spore masses on stems - the macroscopic manifestation of the exact microscopic structures seen in the test image.
